title: Murtaugh
novel:
Barney [[declared|declare]] a new rule: the "Murtaugh." Named after the character from Lethal Weapon, it meant "I'm too old for this [[stuff|stuff]]." Barney [[refused|refuse]] to do anything he considered too young for him.

"No more all-nighters, no more [[excessive|excessive]] drinking, no more [[reckless|reckless]] behavior," Barney [[announced|announce]].

Ted [[disagreed|disagree]]. "We're not old. We can still [[party|party]] like we're twenty."

So Ted [[challenged|challenge]] himself to prove Barney wrong. He tried to pull an all-nighter, go clubbing, and drink until dawn. By midnight, he was [[exhausted|exhaust]]. By 2 AM, his back [[ached|ache]]. By 3 AM, he [[conceded|concede]].

"Okay," Ted [[admitted|admit]]. "Maybe Barney has a point."

Meanwhile, Marshall [[coached|coach]] Lily's kindergarten basketball team. He was [[overly|overly]] [[competitive|competitive]], screaming at five-year-olds to play harder. Lily was [[mortified|mortify]].

"They're five!" she [[protested|protest]].

"They need to learn [[discipline|discipline]]," Marshall [[insisted|insist]].

Barney, despite his Murtaugh rule, could not resist joining the fun. He [[sneaked|sneak]] into a college party and [[ended|end]] up [[injured|injure]] — he tripped on the stairs and [[sprained|sprain]] his ankle.

"I'm too old for this stuff," Barney [[groaned|groan]], [[rubbing|rub]] his ankle.

Ted [[nodded|nod]]. "Welcome to the club."

stuff.en: things in general, without being specific

excessive.en: too much, more than is reasonable

party.en: to celebrate with food, drink, and fun

concede.en: to admit that you have lost

admit.en: to agree that something is true

overly.en: too much, more than is needed

insist.en: to say firmly that something is true

sneak.en: to go somewhere quietly and secretly

end.en: to finish in a particular way

sprain.en: to damage a joint by twisting

groan.en: to make a low sound of pain

rub.en: to move your hand over something

nod.en: to move your head up and down
